ety.text: From Ancient Greek μῦ (mû), derived from Phoenician 𐤌𐤌 (mm /⁠mem⁠/, “water”). Doublet of mem.
From Japanese 無 (mu, “nothing, neither yes nor no”).

senses.d: The 12th letter of the Modern Greek alphabet.

ex: A monk once asked Master Joshu, 'Has a dog the Buddha Nature or not?' Joshu said, 'Mu!'

senses.d: Nothingness; nonexistence; the illusory nature of reality.
ex: That being the case, we should naturally choose to contemplate mu from morning to night, forgetting everything.
Consequently, though mu is mindlike, the likeness to individual consciousness cannot be pushed very far.

senses.d: A unit of surface area, currently equivalent to two-thirtieths of a hectare.
ex: Of 114 village farming families, only ten had more than 30 mu of land and only five had more than 60 mu.

chain.g: The star ο Ceti in the constellation Cetus.

ety.text: From Latin mi(ra) in the hymn for St. John the Baptist.
